Interview: Bitcoin And Black America With Isaiah Jackson

Joe Rodgers
By Joe Rodgers
February 4, 2021
Share

...

On this episode of the “Bitcoin Magazine Podcast,” I had the opportunity to sit down for an interview with Isaiah Jackson to discuss his upcoming book, “Bitcoin And Black America Volume 2.”
Before the interview I read a copy of his first book which laid the groundwork explaining Bitcoin to noobs, though it was written especially for black people. The book covers monetary history and how black people have gotten little to no support from bankers here in America, and goes on to make the case that Bitcoin for black people is a no brainer. As Jackson says, “If any group of people should recognize how media can misrepresent you because they feel threatened, it should be the black community. Bitcoin and the black community are a match made in heaven.”
Aside from his writing, Jackson has been on a mission of Bitcoin outreach. He has big plans in store for 2021, which include a summer camp for Bitcoin education and even a tour around the U.S. visiting with black church leaders. He and Russ Okung are working on that project and I am very interested to see the outcomes.

Bitcoin and Black America

Bitcoin & Black America is Isaiah Jackson's independently published 2019 book arguing that Bitcoin education , ownership and entrepreneurship can support Black economic empowerment. It connects monetary history, banking exclusion, jobs, businesses and community institutions with practical participation in Bitcoin and the broader digital-asset economy.

# Who is Isaiah Jackson?

March 11th, 2023 /

[People profiles](https://www.bitstamp.net/learn/people-profiles/)

Isaiah Jackson is a Bitcoin educator, speaker, and author of the book, “Bitcoin & Black America.” Jackson’s work explores racial discrimination in the traditional banking system and how Bitcoin can help close the wealth gap in underrepresented communities.

Who is Isaiah Jackson?

Jackson views [Bitcoin](https://www.bitstamp.net/learn/cryptocurrency-guide/what-is-bitcoin-btc/) as a tool for economic freedom and is a proponent for self-custody and self-reliance within the ecosystem.

...

After learning more about the crypto space, he decided to become a Bitcoin consultant and trader.

### Bitcoin and Black America

When Jackson started consulting on crypto, he realized that 90% of his clients were Black. Jackson saw the need to present information on blockchain, investing, and crypto fundamentals all in one

...

He wanted to explore the economic injustices faced by various groups and how Bitcoin can positively impact communities of color.

“Bitcoin & Black America” was published in 2019 and received significant attention during the global George Floyd protests in the summer of 2020.
